criteria.criterion: A new file docs/design/direct-main-single-commit-landing.md describes retiring the long-lived local landing branch and building each job's single landing commit on fetched host main by a three-way merge from the job's recorded base. It explains how this removes the landing-and-rebuild wait (2310.0 of 2342.1 median minutes per landed job).
criteria.evidence: The new file's section 1 gives the steps: fetch main, take P from Verified::base(), run merge_tree(P, ours, C), run commit_tree on the fetched tip, push, write one landing record, and keep the local branch as a follower. Section 2 explains the effect: no carried commits, and the 'newest record that lists the job' becomes the first record. It cites 2310.0 of 2342.1, which matches the bottleneck text in evidence records/throughput-reviews/2026-11/20261113-190159-mapn.json.

criteria.criterion: The design has an Existing code section that reuses or extends crates/athena-git/src/lib.rs, crates/athena-core/src/land.rs and docs/design/direct-main-merge-tree-landing.md. It names the functions it builds on and what changes. It names Verified::base() as the source of the base, and says dispatched_from and refuse_detached are only branch checks.

findings.summary: The note leaves out plan's governed-content gate. plan does not three-way merge whenever head differs from the base: if governed content changed between the base and head, it returns Stale.
findings.evidence: In land.rs:176-196, merge_tree runs only when fingerprint(head, p) == fingerprint(p, p). Otherwise plan returns Plan::Stale ('governed content changed on the branch since dispatch'). So if main is passed as head, any job whose governed files changed on main after dispatch goes stale and needs re-verification; it does not merge. Section 6 covers only line conflicts that make merge_tree return None. The earlier note, direct-main-merge-tree-landing.md:166-167, does state this case. The gate is existing behavior, so the design still works, but its conflict and risk analysis is incomplete for the owner and the implementer.

summary: The candidate passes. It adds docs/design/direct-main-single-commit-landing.md, one CHANGELOG entry and decision D178, which is appended to the end of docs/decisions.md. Those are the three expected deliverables. The note proposes retiring the long-lived local landing branch and building one commit per job on fetched host main, using Git::merge_tree from Verified::base(). I checked its code claims against the snapshot and they hold. land.rs:133 reads `let p = verified.base()`. dispatched_from and refuse_detached (land.rs:86 and 105) only read or require a branch. plan returns OtherBranch for a wrong or detached branch and Stale when !is_ancestor(p, head) (land.rs:135-163). The git helpers it names, land_pr, close_carried_prs and stale_seed all exist. The figures 2310.0, 2342.1 and 5.0 match review record 20261113-190159-mapn in the evidence snapshot. The 5.0-minute saving is labeled an estimate and has one scoring basis: the THROUGHPUT.md median compared with 2337.1. The note lists four alternatives, the risks and the failure path, and it says an implementing change must cite the review id. The diff touches only docs. Athena recorded passing fmt and clippy (skipped as docs-only) and a passing cargo test reused from CI for this commit, so nothing needed rerunning. One minor finding: the note leaves out plan's governed-content gate, described below. Owner review is still needed: by the outcome-check default, a fresh reader must rate the note at least 4 of 5, and nothing computes that rating yet.
